newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - March 13.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - March 13.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Prime Minister John Howard yesterday launched an attack on the super industry over the Federal Government's A$1.5 billion superannuation surcharge, saying funds were motivated by self-interest in trying to destroy the surcharge. Doubts were raised over the plan's constitutional legitimacy and Federal Treasurer Peter Costello admitted the Government would seek further legal advice on the matter. Page 1.

The Australian Democrats industrial relations spokesman Senator Andrew Murray said yesterday the party would monitor the Federal Government's new individual workplace agreements to ensure the enforcement of safeguards for employers and employees. Murray tated that enforcement of the legislative protections to ensure fairness would rely on the resources provided to the Employment Advocate office by the Government. Page 4.

A compromise plan being developed for the Prime Minister, John Howard, on the Wik High Court decision is likely to be rejected by at least three State governments next Thursday. A special Premiers meeting, to be held before the Premiers Conference, will discuss the plan, with Western Australia, Queensland and the Northern Territory unlikely to accept draft provisions. Page 5.

Senator Richard Alston, the Federal Minister for Communications, has rejected concerns that media proprietor Mr Kerry Packer should not be permitted to own the John Fairfax Holdings newspaper group due to his interest in gambling. This is an indication that the Federal Government intends to change current rules regarding media ownership. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Communications Minister Richard Alston said yesterday he did not expect Kerry Packer's interests in casinos would prohibit him from bidding for the Fairfax newspaper group when the Federal Government's cross-media ownership rules are announced in the nextfew weeks. Alston added that Rupert Murdoch, a U.S. citizen, would have more trouble convincing the Federal Government that News Limited should increase its stake in the Seven Network. Page 1.

The latest six-monthly survey into investments conducted by Access Economics has found that investment in Australian wines are successful, with the price of local wines going through the roof, offering the most attractive investment of the past five years Coin collectors and taxi plate owners in Melbourne and Sydney have also fared well, but investments in thoroughbreds of rural lands have gone backwards. Page 1.

The Sharpening Their Future report into the New South Wales schooling system by leading educationalist Professor Barry McGaw has suggested the tertiary entrance ranking should be dumped and Year 12 students should be able to study university subjects whil still at school. Federal and State education ministers will look at the proposals when they meet in Melbourne tomorrow. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard admitted to Liberal Party supporters in Victoria yesterday that economic growth must accelerate to a rate of about four or 4.5 per cent to ensure a reduction in the jobless rate. Howard's admission indicates that with Budget foecasts of economic growth at 3.5 per cent until the end of the century, the Government expects unemployment to stay around 8.5 per cent well into the future. Page 1.

THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD An 18-month review of New South Wales' system for the final years of schooling, released yesterday by State Education Minister John Aquilina, recommended the Tertiary Entrance Rank, used by universities to select students, should be replaced by a more fleible system, and also recommended the number of Year 12 courses be dropped. Page 1.

Following an announcement by New South Wales Police Commissioner Peter Ryan that the State's Police Special Branch will be disbanded, fears have arisen over the security of highly sensitive police files on politicians, judges, barristers and civil libertaians. The Opposition has called for all files on politicians to be placed in the hands of the Independent Commission Against Corruption. Page 1.

A new analysis for the Higher School Certificate review by Professor Barry McGaw states that leading private and selective schools have been dumping poor-performing students at the end of Year 10 while recruiting replacements likely to boost their overallHSC results. Page 1.

Tasmania Councillor Neil Noye, the local mayor of the Port Arthur area, said the future of the Broad Arrow Cafe, where 20 people were killed by gunman Martin Bryant last year, may be announced on the anniversary of the massacre on April 28. Only the stone walls and floor remain of the cafe, and the remains may be buried rather than being razed or kept as a memorial. Page 3.
THE AGE

As the Institute of Chartered Accountants warned yesterday that a survey found at least 60,000 people would be advised to change their super plans and divert funds into more attractive investments under the Federal Government's planned 15 per cent surchare on high-income earners' super contributions, the Federal Government has gone to the Attorney-General's Department to seek further legal advice on the plan, which may be in breach of the Constitution. Page A1.

Victorian auditor-general Mr Ches Baragwanath has stated that he will resign if the Victorian Government proceeds with a proposal to bypass his office in changes resulting from the Government's review of the Audit Act. Under the new provisions, Governmen departments will be allowed to select their own auditors. Page A1.

The Federal Minister for Communications, Senator Richard Alston, said yesterday that it was not essential to have multiple media owners to achieve a diversity of views. New media ownership rules will be released in coming weeks. Page A1.

Victorian transport workers met yesterday in the first of a series of stopwork meetings to defy Government warnings by endorsing the weekend union strike and approving moves to increase industrial action. A tactical campaign will be developed today by unon delegates which is expected to disrupt public transport schedules and interrupt electricity supplies. Page A3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373 1800
